evidence.detail: R302 InterfaceRenderer iterates active rs/l/e/f instances during live widget traversal and queries each controller by the current RSInterface.aw widget id before dispatching any registered R314 InterfaceWidgetRenderCallback.

Each rs/l/e/f instance owns the int-keyed registry of rs/l/e/i callbacks. Protected registration helpers bind either one widget id or an int[] of widget ids to a callback, making the class the controller-side owner of feature-specific widget render behavior.

Only rs/l/e/f instances with non-empty callback registries are admitted to the list consumed by InterfaceRenderer, so the class participates directly in activation and render dispatch rather than merely storing callback data.

The exact-v308 recovered-source inventory places rs/l/e/f beside the concrete rs/l/e/a/* feature controllers and records imports of the concrete controller family plus GamblingInterface, consistent with the shared feature-controller role independently exposed by the R314 dispatch path.

proposals.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the shared interface feature controller that owns widget-id callback registration and participates in InterfaceRenderer dispatch; original stripped source identifier is not claimed.
